strengths: The paper addresses an important efficiency bottleneck: the visual tokens processed by the language model. Combining image-adaptive selection with token merging is a simple, potentially useful design that requires little architectural modification.

Evaluation covers six image benchmarks, two language-model sizes, and three video benchmarks. PruMerge+ demonstrates a useful tradeoff at the reported 25% token budget: the 7B model retains 76.8 versus 78.5 VQAv2 accuracy and achieves 64.9 versus 64.3 on MMBench.

The video experiments provide encouraging evidence of deployment without additional training. PruMerge improves ActivityNet-QA accuracy from 45.3 to 48.3 while largely preserving performance on the other two video benchmarks.

The ablations provide evidence beyond comparisons with the original model. Table 4 shows improvements over uniform spatial sampling, Table 5 supports the contribution of merging, and Table 6 distinguishes inference-only application from LoRA adaptation. Foundational methods and benchmark datasets are cited.
weaknesses: The comparisons do not adequately establish the contribution over existing token-reduction techniques. Table 4 considers first-N and uniform spatial sampling, but omits adaptations of the cited token-merging methods and a fixed-budget top-k attention baseline. Consequently, the benefit of adaptive IQR selection over simpler attention selection remains unclear. Comparisons at matched token budgets and training conditions are particularly important because the method combines established attention, outlier-detection, and clustering components.

The practical acceleration claims remain insufficiently validated. Table 2 explicitly reports roofline-model estimates for LLM prefill rather than measured system performance. It does not establish latency including visual encoding and pruning/merging overhead, generation performance, or batching behavior with variable token counts. PruMerge+, which offers the strongest image accuracy tradeoff, also lacks a corresponding efficiency evaluation. The estimates support potential savings but cannot establish their realized magnitude.

Important implementation details are ambiguous or inconsistent. Algorithm 1 adds m spatially sampled tokens to m selected tokens, implying approximately 11% retention when PruMerge retains 5.5%, rather than the reported 25% for PruMerge+. The cluster size k and attention-head aggregation are unspecified, while the update described as weighted averaging lacks an explicit normalization and excludes the center from its listed neighbors. These details affect both the token budget and resulting representations, limiting reproducibility of the central results.

The strongest performance-preservation claims overstate the evidence. In Table 1, 7B PruMerge reduces VQAv2 from 78.5 to 72.0, POPE from 85.9 to 76.3, and MME from 1510.7 to 1350.3 despite additional fine-tuning. These losses may be acceptable for substantial compression, but they do not support claims of uncompromised performance. Section 4.1 also incorrectly claims improvement on POPE. The stronger PruMerge+ results establish a different operating point; broader accuracy-versus-budget comparisons are needed to characterize the claimed tradeoff.
